stem: Which of the following is considered a 'red flag' when monitoring a child with macrocephaly?

options.text: A head circumference that follows the $75^{\text{th}}$ percentile consistently.
An increase in head circumference of more than $2\text{ cm}$ in a single month.
A head circumference that matches the father's head circumference.
The head circumference plateauing after the first year of life.

explanation: Rapid expansion at this rate typically indicates a pathological accumulation of fluid (CSF) or blood.
rationale: Look for a specific rate of growth that suggests something other than standard tissue expansion.

optionExplanations.A: Consistently following a high percentile is often normal; it is the rapid change in trajectory that is concerning.
optionExplanations.B: Rapid expansion at this rate typically indicates a pathological accumulation of fluid (CSF) or blood.
optionExplanations.C: This often suggests benign familial macrocephaly, which is a non-pathological finding.
optionExplanations.D: Plateauing and following a curve after an initial rise is characteristic of benign familial macrocephaly.

originalCorrectOptionTexts: An increase in head circumference of more than $2\text{ cm}$ in a single month.
